claim_text: The Antikythera mechanism is a geared bronze device.
The Antikythera mechanism was recovered from a shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera.
The Antikythera mechanism was recovered in 1901.
The astrolabe projected the celestial sphere onto a flat plate using stereographic projection.
The astrolabe has a rotating star map called the rete.
Medieval Islamic and European astronomers used the astrolabe to tell time.
The lead-acid battery was invented by French physicist Gaston Planté.
The lead-acid battery was invented in 1859.
The lead-acid battery is the oldest type of rechargeable battery.
A lithium-ion cell moves lithium ions between a graphite anode and a metal oxide cathode during charge and discharge.
Lithium cobalt oxide is an example of a metal oxide cathode in a lithium-ion cell.
Lithium-ion cells have a nominal voltage of about 3.6 to 3.7 volts.
Voyager 1 was launched by NASA.
Voyager 1 was launched on September 5, 1977.
Voyager 1 flew past Jupiter in 1979.
Voyager 2 launched on August 20, 1977.
Voyager 2 launched sixteen days before its twin Voyager 1.
Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus.
Tardigrades are microscopic animals.
Tardigrades are typically about 0.5 millimeters long.
Tardigrades have eight legs.
Most extremophiles are microorganisms.
Archaea are an example of extremophile microorganisms.
Most extremophiles live permanently in extreme habitats like hydrothermal vents.
The Rosetta Stone was found in 1799.
The Rosetta Stone was found by French soldiers.
The Rosetta Stone was found at Rashid in the Nile Delta.
Linear B is a syllabic script.
Linear B was used to write Mycenaean Greek.
Arthur Evans found large numbers of Linear B tablets at Knossos on Crete.
CRISPR sequences were first found in bacteria.
In bacteria, CRISPR sequences work as an adaptive immune system against viruses.
In CRISPR gene editing, a guide RNA directs the Cas9 enzyme to a matching DNA sequence.
Kary Mullis invented the polymerase chain reaction in 1983.
Each polymerase chain reaction (PCR) cycle includes a denaturation step at about 94 to 98 °C.
Each polymerase chain reaction (PCR) cycle includes a primer annealing step.
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapsed on November 7, 1940.
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapsed into Puget Sound.
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapsed only four months after it opened.
London's Millennium Bridge opened on June 10, 2000.
London's Millennium Bridge closed two days after it opened.
London's Millennium Bridge closed because it swayed sideways under crowds.
John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and William Shockley built the first working point-contact transistor.
The first working point-contact transistor was built at Bell Labs.
The first working point-contact transistor was built in 1947.
A vacuum tube controls current by emitting electrons from a heated cathode through a vacuum to a plate.
John Ambrose Fleming invented the vacuum tube diode in 1904.
Lee de Forest added a control grid to the vacuum tube to create the triode in 1906.
The Panama Canal is about 82 kilometers long.
The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
The United States completed the Panama Canal in 1914.
The Suez Canal opened in 1869.
The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
The Suez Canal is about 193 kilometers long.
Bi Sheng invented movable type.
Bi Sheng's movable type was made of baked clay.
Bi Sheng invented movable type in China.
Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable metal type printing.
Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable metal type printing in Mainz.
Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable metal type printing around 1440.
The Enigma machine was invented by German engineer Arthur Scherbius.
The Enigma machine was invented at the end of World War I.
The Enigma machine encrypted letters with a set of rotating rotors.
The Lorenz SZ40/42 enciphered teleprinter messages.
The Lorenz SZ40/42 enciphered messages by adding a pseudorandom keystream.
The Lorenz SZ40/42 keystream was generated by 12 wheels.
Apollo 13 launched on April 11, 1970.
Apollo 13 carried astronauts Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise.
About 56 hours into the flight, an oxygen tank in the Apollo 13 service module exploded.
Apollo 11 launched on July 16, 1969.
Apollo 11 carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins.
Apollo 11's Lunar Module Eagle landed on July 20, 1969.
